prompts.Warship:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: first static master render for a top-down historical RTS game, Age of Fronts, Russian culture Stone Age boats. Image 1 is ONLY a rendering-style, detail-quality and directly-overhead camera reference, NOT a vessel design to copy.
Make exactly ONE complete vessel, isolated on true transparent RGBA background, square canvas. Pure orthographic view from straight above, camera perpendicular to the deck, bow points precisely screen-up. No perspective, no isometric angle, no visible vertical exterior hull sides. Paint in the polished semi-realistic game-art style of the reference, with crisp large material shapes, restrained fine detail, warm carved wood, convincing thickness and clean contact shadows within the vessel. Soft consistent upper-left lighting. Fill 84% of canvas height with the vessel including paddles, keep generous transparent margin, center its mass on the canvas center. No water, no wake, no floating shadow outside the hull, no scenery, no labels, no UI, no crew. The user needs to read the ship's ROLE at 24â€“48 screen pixels: prioritize the main silhouette and only a few big, recognizable objects over decoration.
Regional prehistoric inspiration from forest/lake and river communities of the eastern European plain: hollowed log timber, visible hand-tool marks, simple split-wood beams, bast cord lashings, animal hides, leaf-bladed wooden paddles and earthy ochre. This is a gameplay concept grounded in regional materials, not a claim of a recovered vessel class. No Russian national flags, stars, crosses, heraldry, medieval shields or shield bosses, Viking dragon prows, iron, bronze, nails, guns, sails, masts, fabric pennants, tropical outriggers, modern ropes, planked clinker longships or fantasy ornament. The exposed joining and equipment must be physically connected and practical. No clipped paddles or ambiguous disconnected parts.
Subject and role: RUSSIAN STONE AGE WARSHIP, a slender, fast river fighting canoe. One single hollowed oak log with pointed bow, a narrow oval interior, thick continuous carved wooden gunwales, and three simple crosswise timber seats. Strong slender spearhead-like overall silhouette, roughly 3.5 times longer than wide when including the stowed paddles. Two large stone-tipped hunting/fighting spears firmly lashed parallel along the upper outer gunwales, their tips pointing toward the bow and clearly separated from the boat. Two broad dark reddish-ochre hide wraps over the gunwales at midships give large readable combat accents, not shields. Four leaf-bladed wooden paddles are stowed flush alongside, securely lashed in matched pairs and do not extend dramatically beyond the hull. Empty open fighting space, absolutely no cargo baskets, sacks or tent. Clear evidence of ONE dugout hull, no metal fittings, no canopy. Keep the combat silhouette sharp and purposeful, readable as combat even in grayscale.

Subject and role: RUSSIAN STONE AGE TROOP TRANSPORT, a sturdy broad river passenger craft, clearly differentiated from a cargo boat and combat canoe. A single broad oval hollowed-log hull, blunt gently rounded bow and stern, substantial continuous carved log gunwales, about 2.3 times longer than wide including the stowed paddles. Five thick pale split-wood passenger benches spaced evenly across the open dark interior, producing five big readable horizontal stripes from overhead. The center is entirely open seating, no cargo, no crates, no sacks, no pottery, no weapons, no canopy. Broad pale rawhide pads on the two end seats, restrained visible bast bindings for the paddle lash points; a pair of substantial long leaf-bladed paddles stowed neatly along the outside sides. Carved wood supports the benches realistically. Practical prehistoric passenger capacity conveyed by a broad rounded body and repeated empty benches, not decorative details.

Subject and role: RUSSIAN STONE AGE TRADE BOAT, a wide, stable inland cargo craft. Two SHORT robust hollowed-log pontoons in parallel, joined securely by four visible crosswise split-timber beams and bast rope lashings, supporting a broad low rectangular cargo platform. The outline is compact and almost rectangular, about 1.6 times longer than wide, with two rounded bow tips clearly readable at screen-top. This twin-log cargo configuration is a gameplay interpretation; make its construction genuinely plausible. Cover most of the deck with ONLY six large, strongly separated cargo masses: two golden woven bark/reed baskets, two pale hide-wrapped packages, one reddish clay pot with a wide visible dark opening, and one rolled dark brown fur bundle. No modern square wooden crates, no tiny scatter of dozens of items. Each bundle is secured with substantial crossed bast cord bindings. A short bare workspace at stern with two stowed wooden paddles. No weaponry, no shields, no sail, no canopy, no leafy green adornment. The big light and golden cargo shapes and broad twin-hull silhouette should instantly read as commerce, contrasting with empty bench rows of the transport and long narrow war canoe.
prompts.TradeV2: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this existing transparent top-down cargo boat master for a historical RTS game. Keep the exact overhead orthographic camera, screen-up bow, polished painterly material style, lighting, and the same six large cargo objects (two woven baskets, two pale hide packages, one reddish clay pot, one dark fur bundle), secured lashings and two stowed stern paddles. CHANGE ONLY THE VESSEL PROPORTIONS: make the outer hull/deck substantially broader and more compact, with total length to width about 1.6:1, rather than this long narrow 2.3:1 outline. Set its visible outer bounds approximately 70â€“72% of the square canvas height and 44â€“46% of the canvas width, centered on the canvas. Separate the two solid-log pontoons laterally with much longer transverse beams; make a wider low wooden cargo platform that supports the original six cargo masses in two columns of three, with a modest gap between the columns. Repaint the enlarged wood and basket forms naturally, never stretch texture pixels. Keep the cargo secure and actually resting on the deck, keep split-wood beam connections and bast lashings physically connected, with a stern paddle workspace. Short stout raft-like outline, twin rounded bow tips, broad and clearly distinguishable from a thin fighting canoe or single-hull passenger boat at 24â€“48 pixels. No new objects, canopy, sail, mast, weapons, flags, crew, water, wake, shoreline, UI, text, or background. True transparent RGBA background with pristine empty transparent outer margins, no stray speckles. This is still a static master only, not a sprite sheet.
